A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LlavaGuard work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v3 retains Appendices A–J and adds Appendix K. The material supports reliable comparison, including relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original safety-benchmark evaluations, large-scale dataset and generated-image audits, ablations, and human-agreement results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds model comparisons, quantitative rationale evaluation, downstream ImageNet experiments, and failure-case analysis.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds QwenGuard-3B and QwenGuard-7B using Qwen2.5-VL backbones alongside the existing Llava-OneVision variants. The taxonomy, policy augmentation, guided-rationale construction, and structured assessment procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The safety dataset and existing real and synthetic audit coverage are retained. Section 7.1 adds downstream ImageNet object classification using original versus safety-filtered training data, extending task coverage beyond image-safety assessment. Newly disclosed annotator demographics do not establish a population change.

E2.justification: The held-out comparison expands substantially from v2 Table 2 to v3 Table 3: it adds InternVL2.5 at 1B/8B/78B, Qwen2.5-VL at 3B/7B/72B, QVQ-72B-Preview, and the fine-tuned Siglip2Guard baseline. Existing comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces two substantial evaluation designs: GPT-4o scoring dataset rationales on a 1–10 scale, and controlled ResNet-50 training on unfiltered versus filtered ImageNet. The latter uses 50 epochs, AdamW, learning rate 0.001, and top-1/top-5 evaluation overall and on the ten most heavily filtered classes. Existing safety splits and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds guided-versus-base rationale and generator-size analyses (Table 2), downstream filtering utility and class-specific impact analysis (Section 7.1), and false-positive analysis addressing boundary ambiguity and embedded text (Appendix K, Figure 13). Existing ambiguity, policy, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports ± quantities for the downstream ImageNet accuracies in Section 7.1. Their statistical meaning and the number of runs or seeds are unspecified, so this establishes added uncertainty reporting but not a documented increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Existing matched benchmark and human-agreement values are retained. Substantial new results include comparator scores, QwenGuard-3B/7B balanced accuracies of 88.72%/89.71%, and guided/base Llava-34B rationale means of 9.1/3.8. Within v3's filtering experiment, unfiltered/filtered top-1 accuracy is 67.2%/67.4% overall but 53.6%/46.9% on the ten most heavily filtered classes. These are added results, not revised same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The Policy Exception Rate and Policy Exception Score definitions, including Equations 1–2 and the harmonic-mean formulation, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of an open safeguarding framework, customizable taxonomy, annotated dataset, flexible policy adherence, superior safety performance, and dataset/model auditing applications. The new evaluations support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 adds the qualification that stable aggregate recognition accuracy can conceal losses in heavily filtered classes. The limitations and Appendix K identify decision-boundary and embedded-text failures. Appendix J additionally interprets retained human agreement in light of demographic differences between annotators and participants.

D1.justification: Appendices I–J newly disclose annotator and participant demographics and consensus handling of ambiguous annotations. v3 also supplies training settings for the new ResNet experiment. Existing LlavaGuard training, hardware, and oversampling details remain. The access pointer changes from the repository to a project page; public training resources were already described in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Bai et al. (2023) on Qwen-VL and Tschannen et al. (2025) on SigLIP 2, supporting the added models. The broader positioning relative to existing safeguards, general-purpose VLMs, and rigid NSFW classifiers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 introduces numbered subsections throughout Sections 3–7, makes local language corrections, updates affiliation and publication information, and reorders acknowledgements and the impact statement. The main narrative and section sequence are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds rationale Table 2 and failure-case Figure 13, expands and reformats the main comparison as Table 3, and replaces the former human-agreement table with unchanged values in prose. Figure 8 rearranges the same examples from a four-by-three to a two-by-six grid. Other displays are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 lacked a quantitative guided-rationale comparison and a downstream test of dataset filtering. v3 adds both, substantially strengthening support for central framework components, while broader baseline comparisons reinforce the performance evidence. Reporting class-specific accuracy losses and concrete false positives also makes applicability limits clearer. These address important validation gaps, although undefined ± quantities and incomplete details for some new experiments remain weaknesses.
